title: Weak proper-power-aware fourth-moment bound at the binary Hayes endpoints
statement: Let ell>=200 and n be 2 ell+1 or 2 ell+2. Put mu=2^(n-ell), D_e=N_n(e)-mu, M_4=sum_e D_e^4, and let P_n be one at the odd endpoint and the proved square-plus-higher-power upper bound at the even endpoint. Then M_4<(mu-P_n)^4.

provenance.source: Axeyum gf2-lemire lane; corrected weak fourth-moment implication after the ten-lens blocker sweep

notes: This is the current weakest recorded aggregate target that preserves the repository's proved proper-power subtraction. The weaker-looking M_4<2^(4(n-ell)) proves only positive Mangoldt mass and still permits N_n(1)=1 at the odd endpoint, so it is not sufficient. The native ledger proves the implication and reports both the exact rational R_0 allowance and the exact constant allowed in the Hast--Matei normalization M_4<=C*2^ell*mu^3. The published theorem fixes n,h, permits C to depend on them, takes q to infinity, and excludes p=2 for m=4; the missing route is therefore a degree-uniform wild characteristic-two fourth moment, not merely removal of the tameness hypothesis. At ell=200 the allowed log2 root ratios are approximately 171.482426 and 173.482426, versus the older target R_0<=4. Finite distributions are controls only.
